title: Finding a Healthy Weight
hook: BMI is a quick screen, not a verdict. A healthy weight is the range where your risk of disease stays low — and your waistline tells part of the story too.
key_points: A healthy weight is the range linked to lower risk of weight-related disease.
BMI is a rough screening tool from height and weight — useful, but limited.
BMI can mislead for muscular people and doesn't show where fat sits.
Waist size adds information: fat around the belly carries more health risk.
content_html: "Healthy weight" sounds like a single magic number, but it's really a range — the weight band where your risk of weight-related diseases stays low. The most common way to screen for it is BMI, calculated from your height and weight. It's handy, but it's a starting point, not the whole picture.
extra_html: The U.S. CDC describes BMI as a screening tool: easy to calculate and useful at the population level, but blunt for individuals. It can't tell muscle from fat, so a very muscular person may land in a high category without excess fat, and it says nothing about where fat sits on the body. That last part matters — fat carried around the abdomen tends to carry more health risk than fat elsewhere, which is why a waist measurement adds something BMI misses. Treat these as conversation-starters with a clinician, who can weigh them alongside your blood pressure, blood sugar, family history, and overall health rather than judging by a number alone.

related.title: Weight Loss That Lasts
related.hook: Crash diets win the first month and lose the year. Slow, steady loss built on habits you can actually keep is what stays off.

related.title: Building a Balanced Plate
related.hook: Forget counting every calorie — the simplest healthy-eating tool is a picture of a plate: half produce, a quarter grains, a quarter protein.

related.title: Preventing Type 2 Diabetes
related.hook: Type 2 diabetes often arrives slowly, with a warning stage called prediabetes — and at that stage, modest lifestyle changes can stop or delay it.

related.title: AI Calorie Apps Missed 250–345 Calories per Meal
related.hook: Snap a photo, get a number — and NIH researchers found that number runs 250 to 345 calories light per meal, with about 30 grams of fat simply unaccounted for.

flashcards.prompt: What is BMI, and what's its main limitation?
flashcards.back_html: BMI is a screening tool calculated from your height and weight. It's a useful rough guide, but it doesn't distinguish muscle from fat or show where fat is stored — so it can mislead for very muscular people.

flashcards.prompt: Why does waist size add useful information beyond BMI?

choices.text: Fat carried around the belly carries more health risk
A larger waist always means lower disease risk

flashcards.explanation_html: The CDC notes that where fat sits matters — extra fat around the abdomen is linked to higher health risk, which BMI alone can't reveal.
